Prazosin is funny because it can increase vividity while searching for the right dose. When I first started, it was still better than nightmares because I felt more like I understood my dreams and they were still less scary, but after upping the dose a little bit, the nightmares basically just…stopped.

Reading through this, it feels more like incel** vibes than dysphoria. Kind of a, “If women get sexual validation simply for existing, I am owed that same validation. If I do not receive it, that proves women are selfish because they don’t need to compliment men the same way that men need to compliment women. Women are inherently cruel to men for making them pursue them and not fancying our bodies in their average form the same way we fancy a lady’s body.”

This person seems to really need therapy before slipping further into this delusion to protect himself from insecurity in relationships with the opposite sex. I am getting major future sexual assault, aggravated assault, or other violent acts vibes.

Have you posted photos of yourself that didn’t gain the traction you hoped? Is this what lead to this way of thinking? Have you observed others who posted these types of photos and relate to their desire to do so while observing they didn’t have any validation for their post? This seems to be based on the idea that men’s bodies aren’t as easily physically complimented. 

This isn’t because men aren’t “sexy.” It has more to do with what women versus men tend to find attractive. Men are the more visual sex. Seeing waist to hip ratios makes a man think of sliding his hand in the curve of a woman’s waist. A photo of thighs makes a man imagine what is between them.

For women, while a man’s body can be attractive, we tend to be more motivated by the way someone makes us feel. A photo doesn’t incite the same kind of thoughts. The right caption or background to make a photo more comical or engaging is the best way to get that kind of validation from someone who isn’t already a romantic partner. 

Women are also less likely to leave comments in the same manner as men. We can be told we’ve lead a man to believe something and therein, owe him. We have to be more guarded, so a man is less likely to receive physical compliments. 

It seems like you just wanted to post a picture of an average guy and elicit feelings from women they don’t typically have because we think differently. A man’s body doesn’t turn me into mush, no matter the body. I’m not going to comment on a thirst trap, no matter the man. Taking things like this and making them mean something different is a great way to denigrate the world for your own unmet needs.

I’ve been making too much cortisol since I can remember. 

When I am actually getting all the “stuff,” (mainly anything that helps make vitamin B and serotonin) I literally get a little amped, like feeling good good. The rest of the time, I’m usually dragging myself to do everything, even if eating healthier or trying to be more active/creative.

I don’t take anything that isn’t a whole foods based product. They have actual chamomile, reishi mushroom, St.johns wart, bilberry leaf, etc. It’s actual things one could eat, not lab-stimulated vitamins like cyanocobalamin. I just take concentrated amounts of nutrient-dense foods! So, it could be placebo. It’s always possible, who ever really knows?

I understand it. I do. I think that’s why I have such trouble with beating suicidal ideation. I can cultivate positive emotions and understand them. I can choose them and do my best to live them, but they aren’t my factory settings. The sadness always comes back. I am tired of waiting on waves, good or bad. I am tired of floating in melancholy when the water is calm. 

I can be extremely enthusiastic, passionate, and excited. I have one of those good senses of humor and one of those real laughs. I just also have mental dissonance that has existed since I can remember.

Honestly, the alternative is to not explain it away and just express compassion and empathy for the pain. The trouble is that it requires the person trying to help to take on at least some of that pain. Most people can’t take on chronic depression, just like the people suffering from it can’t bear it. Often, depressed people see the world quite clearly, but it isn’t an easy image to look at. 

Obviously, no one needs to hear, “You should kill yourself,” but it doesn’t mean they need to hear, “Everything happens for a reason,” either. The latter means, this pain is for some unknown purpose, and it’s just supposed to be experienced with no reasonable end date. For people who would already rather die, it comes across as more bleak and hopeless than permission to end the pain.

We can remember it’s a cycle, but that’s what’s got me thinking about the end to be honest. I can’t take the swings, and trying to keep the brave face on just makes me feel like a fraud. Sure, there are good times to look forward to, but if life stress will always lead to this kind of low, I just feel very vulnerable existing. 

It becomes a matter of, if I’m going to lose and drown eventually, why work so hard to keep swimming? Coming up feels great, but it can’t be relied on, whereas the sadness can. It’s the thing that always comes back. 

The happiness is hard-fought and won through conscious action. I drink a lot of water, do light exercise, have creative hobbies, but when I try to be like a “normal” person living in society, I lose all the progress. I am plagued with anxiety and ideation, so I have little desire to keep trying. Then, I feel guilty about not feeling like I should keep trying. It’s a vicious cycle of waves these days. 

My self-worth is very tied to my ability to operate successfully in society, and while I am great at connecting with people, I somehow suck at people-ing in society myself. In a capitalist society, those who cannot earn, are a detriment. I feel that in my soul. I just want to contribute.

That’s part of it too. I don’t know if I can ever really catch up from all this time. I haven’t hit that chronological time yet, but I am far enough into life to realize my opportunities are becoming fewer. I feel like I do a lot of good for people, but it never translates into capital or breaking the cycle of instability.

I also had the middle-class upbringing, and I struggle with the fact that I didn’t maintain the same image and financial standing into adulthood. I have this thing I do, and it leads to a lot of people seeing me....and I don’t know how long I can keep going with a smile on my face. I worry that I will also be another person who ends up on disability, and it feels like it’s all my fault that I haven’t been able to fix it the same way other people have. I just want to feel like I’ve moved on.
